paper.title_en: <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math>-Process Nucleosynthesis with Ab Initio Nuclear Masses around the <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn></mrow></math> Shell Closure
paper.abstract_en: Our understanding of the origin of heavy elements beyond iron relies on the rapid neutron capture process (<math display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> process), which accounts for roughly half of their cosmic abundance. However, the extreme neutron-rich conditions required for the <math display="inline"><mi>r</mi></math> process involve many nuclei that remain experimentally inaccessible, making theoretical predictions essential. We explore the impact of nuclear masses calculated with the ab initio valence-space in-medium similarity renormalization group, focusing on the region around the <math display="inline"><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn></math> shell closure. We show for the first time that such ab initio mass calculations can be used to refine <math display="inline"><mi>r</mi></math>-process predictions compared to global, but more phenomenological mass models. With the ab initio masses, the waiting point of the second <math display="inline"><mi>r</mi></math>-process peak is strengthened, which leads to an overall slower nucleosynthesis flow, lower abundances of nuclei beyond the peak, and a stronger shift of the third <math display="inline"><mi>r</mi></math>-process peak.
